summary: 429 rate limit errors immediately after first production launch (quota + client retry/backoff guidance needed)
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports frequent HTTP 429 responses immediately after enabling production traffic for Hosted API. They expected “pay-as-you-go will just scale” and were surprised by rate limits/quota constraints and lack of clear guidance on retry/backoff. Traffic spike occurred right after feature flag rollout in their app.

Impact:
- Production launch blocked for ~45 minutes; customer disabled the feature.
- End users saw “Try again later” errors.
- Customer concerned about reliability/SLA expectations for self-serve tier.

Customer details:
- Company: Bluepeak AI
- Plan/tier: Self-serve Hosted API
- Region: us-east-1
- Primary endpoints: /v1/chat.completions (streaming and non-streaming)
- Models: rw-llama-3-70b-instruct (primary), rw-qwen2.5-72b-instruct (fallback)

What changed / timeline (customer-reported):
- 2025-03-10 16:05 UTC: Enabled prod traffic (~120 concurrent users within minutes)
- 2025-03-10 16:08 UTC: First 429s observed; error rate climbed to ~20–35% during bursts
- 2025-03-10 16:20 UTC: Disabled the feature in production

Observed behavior:
- API responds with 429 Too Many Requests.
- Response headers include rate-limit signals; customer did not implement retry/backoff and treated 429 as fatal.
- Customer also mixing streaming and non-streaming calls in tight loops without client-side concurrency limits.

Environment / identifiers:
- Request IDs (examples): req_01HTX4N1Q7K2V0M8K9C9, req_01HTX4P0B8T0K6R2Y1Q3
- Tenant/workspace: bluepeak-prod (ID redacted in ticket)
- User-Agent: Redwood SDK Python/1.21.0 (some calls from OpenAI-compat layer)

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) Create a self-serve tenant with default quotas.
2) Run 50–150 concurrent chat.completions with max_tokens=512, mixed streaming and non-streaming.
3) Observe 429s during burst windows when RPM/TPM or concurrent request caps are exceeded.

Investigation notes:
- Gateway logs show clean auth (no 401/403) and normal upstream latency; errors are policy-enforced throttles.
- Metering/limits appear to be functioning as designed; primary gap is expectation-setting + production-safe client behavior.
- Customer did not configure budgets/alerts and did not review limits in Console prior to launch.

Current limits (as verified in Console at time of triage):
- Default self-serve rate limits applied (exact tenant-specific numbers confirmed in Console; customer was exceeding burst capacity).
- No quota increase request submitted prior to launch.

Recommended mitigation provided to customer:
- Implement exponential backoff with jitter for 429s and honor Retry-After if present.
- Add client-side concurrency caps (especially for streaming).
- Use idempotency keys for safe retries where applicable.
- Consider pinning model and setting fallback policy to reduce cascading retries.
- Configure quota/budget alerts in Console.

Docs/links to share (and to surface in onboarding checklist):
- Rate limits & quotas: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/limits-and-quotas (internal canonical link)
- Retries/backoff guidance: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/reliability/retries-timeouts
- Streaming reliability: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/streaming#disconnects-and-reconnect
- Console usage dashboard expectations (data freshness): https://docs.redwoodinference.com/console/usage

Support ask / requested outcome:
1) Confirm whether limits were correctly enforced and advise if a short-term quota increase is appropriate.
2) Provide an approved snippet for Python and TypeScript to handle 429 with backoff + jitter.
3) Capture as checklist gap: “Review limits + set alerts + add retry/backoff before production.”

Resolution (summary):
- Confirmed throttling was expected given observed burst patterns.
- Granted temporary quota increase for 48 hours to support a controlled relaunch, contingent on implementing backoff + concurrency caps.
- Provided production-ready retry/backoff snippet and pointed customer to docs.
- Logged follow-up for DevEx/Docs/Checklist to make quotas/rate limits unmissable during first production launch.

Follow-ups:
- Add/strengthen checklist step: “Set quotas/budgets + alerts” and “Configure retries/backoff for 429/5xx” with deep links.
- Ensure quickstart examples include 429 handling and streaming concurrency guidance.
- Consider Console nudge when user’s recent traffic hits >80% of limit (out of scope for this support ticket).
comments: 2025-03-10 16:34 UTC — Priya Shah (Support): Acknowledged receipt to customer. Asked for approximate concurrency, whether streaming enabled, and a few request IDs + timestamps. Noted 429s typically indicate enforced limits; will confirm tenant quotas and advise on best practice retries/backoff.

2025-03-10 17:05 UTC — Customer (Bluepeak AI): Peak ~120 concurrent users right after launch. Mix of streaming chat + some non-streaming “summaries.” We did not add retries; we assumed 429 wouldn’t happen on paid usage. Provided request IDs req_01HTX4N1Q7K2V0M8K9C9 and req_01HTX4P0B8T0K6R2Y1Q3 around 16:10–16:18 UTC.

2025-03-10 17:22 UTC — Dev Patel (Support): Checked Console limits for tenant and confirmed bursts exceeded default self-serve caps. Not seeing upstream instability. Suggested immediate fixes: exponential backoff with jitter for 429 + respect Retry-After, add concurrency limit for streaming, and avoid retry storms.

2025-03-10 18:10 UTC — Dev Patel (Support): Shared Python guidance (pseudo-snippet): retry on 429 with exponential backoff + jitter, cap max attempts, and log x-request-id + x-ratelimit-* headers. Recommended adding a client-side semaphore for max concurrent streams. Pointed to internal docs links (limits/quotas + reliability/retries-timeouts).

2025-03-11 09:15 UTC — Dev Patel (Support): Offered temporary quota increase for 48 hours for relaunch window if customer confirms they will implement backoff + concurrency caps. Also recommended setting up budget alerts in Console to avoid surprises.
2025-03-11 10:02 UTC — Customer (Bluepeak AI): Confirmed we’ll implement backoff + a streaming concurrency cap. Please proceed with temporary increase; we’re re-testing later today.

2025-03-11 11:30 UTC — Dev Patel (Support): Temporary quota increase applied (internal change logged in tenant admin). Advised customer to ramp traffic gradually and monitor Console usage dashboard; noted up to a short delay in dashboard aggregation.

2025-03-12 15:40 UTC — Dev Patel (Support): Customer reports successful relaunch with reduced 429 rate after implementing backoff + limiting concurrent streams. Marking ticket resolved. Noted product feedback: this should be a first-class checklist step to prevent launch-day surprises.
resolution: Resolved after confirming 429s were expected due to exceeding default self-serve limits during a bursty launch. Provided recommended retry/backoff + streaming concurrency guidance, shared quota/limits docs, and applied a temporary quota increase to support a controlled relaunch. Follow-up captured for onboarding checklist to surface quotas/budgets/429 handling before first production launch.
